definition: Refurbish means to renovate a worn object or place so it is clean, sound, and usable again.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word refurbish. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know refurbish should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The shop sells refurbished laptops — wiped, retested, fitted with new batteries — for half the price of new ones.
Tidy up is a far lighter pass than refurbish — sweep, dust, straighten, and the room merely looks cared for — while refurbishing makes the place sound and usable again, down to the hinges.
Restore goes further than refurbish — every detail is returned to what the original makers intended, period materials and all, where refurbishing settles for clean, sound, and usable.

Spruce up is surface-level freshening — a scrub, a coat of paint, done by lunch, with nothing behind the walls touched. Refurbish goes deeper: the whole worn object or room comes back to clean, sound, usable condition, down to the wiring if the wiring needs it.

Recondition means to bring a machine back to sound working order — rebuilt motor, fresh seals, tested parts — and it is said mostly of machinery, with function its whole concern. Refurbish covers rooms and furniture as well as machines, and it cares about look and comfort along with working order.

English once had the bare verb furbish — knights furbished their helmets before a parade — but the word rusted away even as refurbish thrived. No other relative descends from forbir, so the only cousin to spot is that ghost: you may still meet furbish in old books, wearing exactly this meaning, minus the again.
Refurbish means to renovate a worn object or place so it is clean, sound, and usable again.

The roadside motel changed hands in March, and by June every room had been refurbished: carpets shampooed, tiles regrouted, mattresses swapped, each lamp rewired and each door eased back onto true hinges.
Nothing about the place became fancy.
It became clean, solid, and pleasant to walk into, which was the whole idea.
Refurbish is the exact word for that summer's work, because it means to restore something to good, clean condition — the object stays itself and gets its usefulness back.
Spruce up stops at the surface, a scrub and a coat of paint; refurbishing goes as deep as the wiring.
Refurbish is for physical things brought back to clean working order: rooms, machines, furniture, fleets.
Its restore-family unit-mates each hold a lane — rejuvenate makes a person or spirit feel young again, recapitulate re-walks the points of an argument, recalibrated trues an instrument to a standard.
Refurbish takes the scrub brush: same object, good to look at and use again, with no claim about youth, accuracy, or argument.

The Bellhaven carousel turned for ninety summers before the town shut it down as unsafe.
A committee voted to refurbish it rather than order a fiberglass replacement.
The work took two winters.
Cracked horses were re-glued and repainted, the motor was rewired, and the platform's soft boards came out one by one.
Volunteers were strict about the goal: not a museum piece, but a machine children could ride daily and parents could trust.
It reopened in May -- the same carousel, sound underfoot, bright to the eye, and certified by the same inspector who had condemned it.
